latin: Paternitas est principium generandi in patre.
translation: Paternity is the principle of generating in the Father.
translation_note: 'Patre' is rendered as the first Trinitarian Person, following the Trinitarian context Edelheit gives the thesis (farmer1998:12486; edelheit2022:15330).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch7, from Latin at farmer1998:12486

sources.text: Henry of Ghent, Quodlibet III, q. 3
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit's identified source: Henry argues there that the Father's own characteristic feature, paternity, is the reason of production, not the divine essence

doctrine: Edelheit reports that the thesis comes from Henry of Ghent's Quodlibet III, question 3, where Henry argues that the Father's own characteristic feature, paternity, is the reason of production, and not the divine essence, although one can say more (paraphrase, edelheit2022:15330).
historiography: Edelheit's chapter is the only scholarship on this thesis found in the material consulted; he quotes the thesis's Latin verbatim from the printed 900 Theses, page 242 (edelheit2022:15357).

quotations.text: paternity is the principle of producing in the Father

not_established: Reception of this thesis beyond Edelheit's chapter, or any discussion of it in Pico's Apologia: not established by the sources consulted.
